case_name: Md. Ashif and others v State of Bihar and others
facts: The appellants were appointed as Voluntary Health Workers in State run dispensaries within the district of Darbhanga in the State of Bihar in June 1985.
In lieu of their services they were paid a monthly honorarium of Rs.50/- only.
They were absorbed as Primary Health Workers by the Chief Medical Officer which carried a pay scale of Rs.535-765.
Their services were terminated by an order dated 20th February, 2001 on the ground that their promotion/absorption as Primary Health Workers was illegal and contrary to the rules.
The termination came pursuant to an enquiry regarding procedure followed in the making of the appointments to class III posts.
issues: Whether the initial appointment of the appellants was illegal
Whether the subsequent absorption as Primary Health Workers was legal
Whether the termination of their services was justified
petitioner_arguments: Their initial appointment was made after a proper advertisement and therefore valid
Their subsequent absorption as Primary Health Workers did not cure any defects in their initial appointment
Their termination was unfair and legally impermissible
respondent_arguments: Their initial appointment was illegal because it was made without following the rules and regulations governing such recruitment
Their subsequent absorption as Primary Health Workers was also illegal because it was based on an irregularity committed 15 years earlier
Their termination was justified because their services were terminated in accordance with the rules
court_reasoning: The law regarding regularization of employees was declared by a Constitution Bench of this Court in Secretary, State of Karnataka & Ors. v. Uma Devi (3) & Ors.
The Court drew a distinction between an irregularity and an illegality in the making of an appointment

In cases where the process itself is completely violative of the Constitutional scheme underlying public employment and no procedure has been followed while granting such appointments, the Court cannot allow such an illegality to continue
Merely because an employee had continued under cover of an order of the court, he would not be entitled to any right to be absorbed or made permanent in the service
holding: The appeals were allowed and the order passed by the learned Single Judge was set aside
The termination of the services of the appellants was held to be illegal
Their initial appointment was found to be irregular but not illegal, and therefore regularization was possible
